content.figure: Figure 10 – Flowchart: Management of patients with cardiogenic shock showing initial assessment for ACS and/or mechanical complications, emergency PCI or surgical treatment, identification/treatment of other causes, consideration of oxygen/ventilatory support (Class I), inotropes/vasopressors (Class IIb), and short-term mechanical circulatory support (MCS, Class IIa); subsequent assessment of improvement in hypoperfusion and organ dysfunction guides weaning or escalation to MCS, renal replacement therapy or palliative care.
content.figure_notes: ACS = acute coronary syndrome; BTT = bridge to transplantation; MCS = mechanical circulatory support; PCI = percutaneous coronary intervention. PCI in ACS, pericardiocentesis in tamponade, mitral valve surgery in papillary muscle rupture. In interventricular septum rupture, MCS as BTT should be considered. Other causes: acute valve regurgitation, pulmonary embolism, infection, acute myocarditis, arrhythmia.
content.management_overview: Management should start as early as possible with early identification and treatment of underlying cause alongside hemodynamic stabilization and organ dysfunction management. Management subdivided into stages (pre-hospital, in-hospital, pre-discharge).
flowchart_key_actions: Assess for ACS and mechanical complications
If ACS/mechanical complication: emergency PCI or surgical treatment
If other causes: identify and treat specifically
Consider oxygen or ventilatory support (Class I)
Assess improvement in hypoperfusion and organ dysfunction
If improved: wean from inotropes/vasopressors and/or MCS and continue aetiological treatment
If not improved: escalate to MCS, renal replacement therapy, or consider palliative care
content.pre_hospital_phase: Acute heart failure (AHF) patients should receive non-invasive monitoring (pulse oximetry, BP, heart rate, respiratory rate) and continuous ECG instituted within minutes of patient contact and in the ambulance if possible.
